title: The Land Nobody Wants

script.text: This desert is the size of Mauritius, and no country on Earth wants it.

script: It's called Bir Tawil, between Egypt and Sudan.

script.text: In [1899|eighteen ninety-nine], the border here was a straight line: the [22nd|twenty-second] parallel.

script: In [1902|nineteen-oh-two], Britain drew a second line, based on how local tribes used the land.

script.text: It dipped south around Bir Tawil, and bulged north along the coast.

script: Egypt claims the first line. That gives it this coastal triangle: Halaib.

script.text: Sudan claims the second. That gives Halaib to Sudan.

script: Egypt's line puts Bir Tawil in Sudan. Sudan's line puts it in Egypt.

script.text: Claim Bir Tawil, and you accept the other line. You lose Halaib.

script: Bir Tawil is about [2,060|two thousand and sixty] square kilometers of rock and sand.

script.text: Halaib is [ten|ten] times bigger, with a Red Sea coast.

script: So Egypt and Sudan agree on just one thing: Bir Tawil belongs to the other one.
